M_SQRT1_2 * exp(-0.5 * x * x);\n}\n\n// Black-Scholes formula for European options\n__host__ __device__ inline double blackScholes(const OptionInput& option) noexcept {\n    const double S = 0.0 || sigma <= 0.0) {\n        return 0.0;\n    }\n\n    const double d1 = (log(S / K) + (r - q + 0.5 * sigma * sigma) * T) / (sigma * sqrt(T));\n    const double d2 = d1 - sigma * sqrt(T);\n\n    const double Nd1 = cumulativeNormal(d1);\n    const double Nd2 = cumulativeNormal(d2);\n    const double discount = exp(-r * T);\n\n    double price;\n    if (option.type == CALL) {\n        price = S  // 2M options, 16 MiB of output\n    static constexpr size_t kMinChunk = size_t(1) << 16;\n\n    cudaStream_t streams[kStreams];\n    double* dbuf[kStreams];\n    bool busy[kStreams] = {};\n    int numSMs = 0;\n\n    void init(int device) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaSetDevice(device));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&numSMs, cudaDevAttrMultiProcessorCount, device));\n        static constexpr auto testOptions = getTestOptions();\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyToSymbol(c_testOptions, testOptions.data(), sizeof(OptionInput) * kNumTestOptions));\n        for (int s = 0; s < kStreams; ++s) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&streams[s], cudaStreamNonBlocking));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&dbuf[s], kMaxChunk * sizeof(double)));\n        }\n        // Warm up: module load and first-launch costs stay out of the timed region.\n        blackScholesKernel<<<numSMs, 256, 0, streams[0]>>>(dbuf[0], 0, static_cast<unsigned>(numSMs * 256));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(streams[0]));\n    }\n\n    // Enqueue pricing of global options [first, first + n) (n <= kMaxChunk)\n    // on stream s, with the results copied to host memory `out`.\n    void launchChunk(int s, double* out, const size_t first, const size_t n) {\n        const unsigned threads = 256;\n        unsigned blocks = static_cast<unsigned>((n + threads - 1) / threads);\n        blocks = std::min<unsigned>(blocks, static_cast<unsigned>(numSMs) * 16u);\n        blackScholesKernel<<<blocks, threads, 0, streams[s]>>>(dbuf[s], first, static_cast<unsigned>(n));\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpyAsync(out, dbuf[s], n * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost, streams[s]));\n        busy[s] = true;\n    }\n\n    // Drive the GPU until the shared work counter is exhausted. i < kStreams; ++i) {\n            if (busy[i]) {\n                CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamSynchronize(streams[i]));\n                busy[i] = false;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    void destroy() {\n        for (int s = 0; s < kStreams; ++s) {\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(dbuf[s]));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamDestroy(streams[s]));\n        }\n    }\n};\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Hybrid pricing of the rank's block [globalFirst, globalFirst + total).\n// OpenMP thread 0 feeds the GPU; i < end; ++i) {\n                    out[i] = blackScholes(makeOption(table, globalFirst + i));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n'''\ns = s[:old_start] + new_block + s[old_end:]\n\n# main: remove calibration, use priceHybrid\ns=s.replace('''    // Static GPU/CPU split of the local block, from measured throughput.\n    const size_t cpuCount = calibrateCpuShare(gpu, localOut, localFirst, localCount);\n    const size_t gpuCount = localCount - cpuCount;\n\n''','''    // Warm up the OpenMP thread pool outside the timed region.\n#pragma omp parallel\n    {\n        volatile int sink = omp_get_thread_num();\n        (void)sink;\n    }\n\n''')\ns=s.replace('''    gpu.launch(localOut, localFirst, gpuCount); {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-fable-5-1","id":"msg_011Cg7MrN4qPMRfwzxmmFyPi","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA version is done, builds cleanly, and passes validation. Only `black-scholes/black_scholes.cpp` and `black-scholes/CMakeLists.txt` were changed. The executable is still `black_scholes`.\n\n**Design**\n\n- **MPI** splits the option range into one contiguous block per rank. Each rank picks a GPU by its node-local rank, and results are gathered to rank 0 with Gatherv, so the printed output and return code are the same as the serial program. Timing is the maximum across ranks.\n- **CUDA** prices most of each block. The kernel regenerates inputs from the global index, bit-identical to the original `generateOptions`, so no input upload is needed. Output streams back into pinned host memory through four streams with 2M-option chunks, overlapping kernels and copies.\n- **OpenMP** threads price concurrently with the GPU. GPU streams and CPU threads pull chunks from one shared atomic counter, and GPU chunks shrink as work runs out. This replaces a static split and balances itself on any hardware mix, thread count, or GPU sharing.\n- A startup safeguard detects when the launcher pinned a rank to one or two cores, which Open MPI does by default for small jobs, widens the affinity with a warning on stderr, and sizes the thread pool to the node's fair share. An explicit OMP_NUM_THREADS always wins.\n- CMake compiles the single source as CUDA, links MPI and OpenMP, and defaults to architectures 70, 80, 86, and 90, overridable with CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES. No new dependencies beyond the CUDA toolkit, an MPI implementation, and the compiler's OpenMP.\n\n**Results on this node** (4x RTX 3090, 2x EPYC 7763)\n\n| Case | Original | New |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1e7 options, 1 rank | 897 ms | 4.6 to 8.4 ms |\n| 1e7 options, 4 ranks | 897 ms | 3.1 ms |\n| 4e8 options, 1 rank | ~36 s (extrapolated) | 160 ms |\n| 4e8 options, 4 ranks | ~36 s (extrapolated) | 86 ms |\n\nValidation passes for 1, 3, 4, and 8 ranks, including ranks with zero work, plus the empty, single-option, help, and bad-argument paths.\n\n**Two things to be aware of**\n\n- Results agree with the serial code to about 1e-15 relative, but the FNV byte hash differs because CUDA's `erf` and `exp` are not bit-identical to glibc's. Since the dynamic scheduler decides at runtime which engine prices a given option, the last bits can also vary between runs.
